_note: Copy to docs/work/checklist/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<subject>.json. Never fill this file in place. status is pass|fail|skipped|substituted; substituted means checked by a different instrument than the item names, and its reason must say which. accepted stays null until a human answers it, so an unfinished run is visibly unfinished. Delete any item whose feature no longer exists rather than skipping it.

run.commit: 57b40f6c (tree for derived facts and the local 1.59.2 pack)
run.data-root: per lane under the session scratchpad (ck/c590, ck/c591, ck/c592, ck/enc, ck/corrupt); ~/.ai-raccoon never opened, port 7721 never bound by this run
run.note: Fix-verification run for 1.59.1 (#872, caller-cancelled tool calls) and 1.59.2 (#874, watch remove wording and missing-key message). Each fix is A/B'd against the release before it: 1.59.0 (nuget, scratch --tool-path) for the 1.59.1 fix, 1.59.1 (nuget, the global tool) for the 1.59.2 fixes. 1.59.2 is tagged on GitHub but not on nuget.org (publish.yml is workflow_dispatch and has not been dispatched for it), so 1.59.2 was packed locally from 57b40f6c and installed into a scratch --tool-path. Items outside those fixes are skipped; the 1.59.0 run covers them.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: status pass, with the note: 'watch remove' of an already-removed path prints 'removed:' again (a no-op, but the wording does not say so)
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: That wording was a defect: the CLI and memory_watch_remove reported a removal that did not happen. 1.59.2 (#874) fixed it.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: 1.59.1: `watch remove <id> <never-watched path>` -> 'removed: .../watch-c591/never-watched', exit 0. 1.59.2: same call -> 'not watched: ... (nothing removed)', exit 0.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: An observed wrong output recorded as a note under pass reads as a pass in a status count. It belonged as status fail, accepted as a known defect with its tracking reference.

Tool 'ai-raccoon' (version '1.59.2') was successfully installed. --version: 1.59.2+57b40f6c333b4d09353750a2ef0f05555f7cbecf. nuget versions end at 1.59.1 for both packages; last publish run 2026-10-18T08:48:45Z (1.59.1).
items.observed-result: The local 1.59.2 build installs and reports the derived version with the tree's commit. The global tool was not updated: 1.59.2 is not on nuget.org, and the global 1.59.1 is the control for the 1.59.2 fixes. The patch step's failure is its self-gate refusing a one-RID shell, which is expected for a one-RID local pack; the unpatched shell already lists osx-arm64.
items.acceptance-reason: Substituted: scratch --tool-path install of a local pack instead of a global force-update from nuget. Version and commit match the tree. Publishing 1.59.2 needs the owner's publish.yml dispatch and production approval.

items.expected-result: A tool call whose HTTP request the client drops mid-flight logs one 914/915 Warning (tool, elapsed ms) and no SDK 'request handler failed' warn with a stack trace; the server stays healthy and the cancelled work stops. Negative control: 1.59.0 logs the SDK warn with its stack trace for the same call (1.59.1 changelog, #872)
items.command: settings ingest scope add <id> <scratch>/corpus (1,968 files copied from docs/ and src/); mcpc.py abort memory_ingest_directory {projectId, path: corpus} 1500 (raw socket POST /mcp, closed after 1,500 ms); wait 8 s; grep the new serve.log lines for 'request handler', '^ *at ', '[91[45]]'; then memory_stats
items.evidence: 1.59.0: 'handler-failed: 1  stack-frames: 23  ev914/915: 1' — warn ToolRefusals[915] '"memory_ingest_directory" timed out after 1528 ms: the caller cancelled it', then warn McpServer[975074943] 'method 'tools/call' request handler failed in 1532.3493ms. System.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledException'. 1.59.1 (nuget): 'handler-failed: 0  stack-frames: 0  ev914/915: 1' — 915 '... timed out after 1528 ms'. 1.59.2: 'handler-failed: 0  stack-frames: 0  ev914/915: 1' — 915 '... timed out after 1510 ms'. memory_stats after: entries 317 (1.59.1), 297 (1.59.2), so ingest stopped at about 300 of 1,968 files and the server answered.
items.observed-result: Fixed on both 1.59.1 and 1.59.2: only the 915 line, no SDK stack-trace warn. The control reproduces the old noise. The 914 rendering (a call with a query) was not driven: no query-bearing tool runs long enough on a scratch bank to cancel.
items.acceptance-reason: Clean A/B on the same call and corpus. 914 shares the code path and is pinned by CancelledRequestLoggingTests and ToolRefusalsCancellationTests.

items.expected-result: `watch remove <id> <path>` on a path with no registration prints 'not watched: <path> (nothing removed)' and exits 0; on a registered path it prints 'removed: <path>'. memory_watch_remove returns removed:false and removed:true in those cases. Negative control: 1.59.1 prints 'removed:' for an unwatched path and has no removed field (1.59.2 changelog, #874)
items.command: settings watch enable <id> true; watch remove <id> <dir> (never watched); watch add <id> <dir>; watch remove <id> <dir>; watch remove <id> <dir> again; MCP memory_watch_remove on an unwatched dir, memory_watch_add, memory_watch_remove; memory_watch_status. Same on 1.59.1 against its own lane server.
items.evidence: 1.59.2 CLI: 'not watched: .../watch-c592/a (nothing removed)' exit=0; after add: 'registered: ...', 'removed: .../watch-c592/a' exit=0; again: 'not watched: ... (nothing removed)' exit=0. 1.59.2 MCP: {"path":".../watch-c592/c","removed":false} then after add {"path":".../watch-c592/c","removed":true}. 1.59.1 CLI never-watched: 'removed: .../watch-c591/never-watched' exit=0. 1.59.1 MCP: {"projectId":...,"path":".../watch-c591/b"} with no removed field, before and after add. memory_watch_status after: {"watches":[]}.

items.acceptance-reason: A/B shows the defect on 1.59.1 and the fix on 1.59.2, for CLI and MCP, with both branches of the removed flag.

items.expected-result: An env-keyed encrypted bank (verifier sidecar present) opened with AIRACCOON_DB_PASSPHRASE unset: `encryption show`, `serve` and `doctor` say the bank is encrypted and no key was resolved, name AIRACCOON_DB_PASSPHRASE, and exit 20 (Key.Unresolved). Controls: the right key opens HEALTHY; a wrong key is still the mismatch (21); a corrupt bank with no verifier is still Bank.Corrupted (32); 1.59.1 shows raw 'SQLite Error 26' (1.59.2 changelog, #874)
items.command: AIRACCOON_DB_PASSPHRASE=<openssl rand -hex 16> 1.59.2 serve --port 0 on a fresh data root, then kill; ls (memory.db.keycheck present; header not 'SQLite format 3'); env -u AIRACCOON_DB_PASSPHRASE <bin> --data-root <enc> encryption show | doctor | serve --port 0 for 1.59.2 and 1.59.1; right-key doctor; wrong-key encryption show; 8 KiB /dev/urandom memory.db with no sidecar -> doctor
items.evidence: 1.59.2 encryption show: "the bank at '.../ck/enc/memory.db' is encrypted, but no encryption key was resolved — set AIRACCOON_DB_PASSPHRASE, or configure the key source this bank uses" exit=20. 1.59.2 serve: 'could not open the bank at ...: the bank ... is encrypted, but no encryption key was resolved — set AIRACCOON_DB_PASSPHRASE ...' exit=20. 1.59.2 doctor: 'doctor: the bank at ... is encrypted, but no encryption key was resolved ...' exit=20, preceded by warn DoctorCommands[1016] '... is not a SQLite database' with SqliteException 'SQLite Error 26' and 9 stack frames. 1.59.1: encryption show 'SQLite Error 26: 'file is not a database'.' exit=32; serve 'could not open the bank ...: SQLite Error 26' exit=32; doctor '... wrong key or corrupt bank ...' exit=32. Right key doctor: 'status: HEALTHY' exit=0. Wrong key: '... its key verifier confirms this key is wrong ...' exit=21. Corrupt, no verifier: '... wrong key or corrupt bank ...' exit=32.
items.observed-result: Fixed for all three commands, and all three controls behave as specified. Residual: doctor still writes its 1016 warn ('is not a SQLite database' plus a 9-frame SqliteException) to the console before the correct message, so the console shows two contradicting diagnoses for one bank.
items.acceptance-reason: The changelog's claims hold, with the control showing the old output. The 1016 warn is noise the changelog did not claim to remove; raised as a follow-up, not a regression.
